newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria lifts ceiling on equity ownership in banks.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria lifts ceiling on equity ownership in banks.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has lifted restrictions on equity ownership by individual and corporate investors in the country's banks, a central bank statement said on Monday.
"The new directive now makes it legal for an individual and/or corporate body to own up to 100 percent shareholding in a bank," the statement said.
Before now, the maximum equity participation of an individual in a bank was 10 percent while that of corporate bodies was 30 percent.
The statement, released in the capital Abuja, said the new law was aimed at assisting banks recapitalise to the new minimum level of 500 million naira.
Finance Minister Anthony Ani announced in the 1997 fiscal budget in January that all banks must recapitalise to the new level, a 900 percent increase from the previous level, by December 1998.
The central bank statement said lifting the ceiling would also encourage credible local and foreign investors to bring additional resources and sound technical management into the banking industry.

Removal of the restrictions was also in keeping with government's economic policy of "guided deregulation" introduced since 1995, and in futherance of the objectives of the country's foreign investment laws, it said.
Government in 1995 revised the investment laws and removed inhibitions on foreigners investing in the economy.
